questions.question: The drainage pattern formed when rivers discharge their waters from all directions in a lake or depression is known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**centripetal.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Drainage Pattern**__

 __
 
• **A drainage pattern is a pattern formed by the streams, rivers, and lakes in a particular drainage basin.**
 
• They are governed by the topography of the land, whether a particular region is dominated by hard or soft rocks, and the gradient of the land.
 
 
 
• **Centripetal**__
 __
 
• **The centripetal drainage pattern is formed when rivers discharge their waters from all directions into a lake or a depression. **
 
• In a low-lying basin, the streams converge from all sides.
 
• **Examples**: streams of Ladakh, Tibet, and the Bagmati and its tributaries in Nepal.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dendritic**__

 __
 
• This is an irregular **tree branch-shaped** pattern.
 
• Drainage is branching or ramifying thereby giving the appearance of a tree.
 
• A dendritic pattern develops in a terrain that has uniform lithology, and where faulting and jointing are insignificant.
 
• **Examples**: Indus, Godavari, Mahanadi, Cauvery, Krishna.
 
 
 
• **Radial **__
 __
 
• **The tributaries from a summit follow the slope downwards and drain down in all directions**.
 
• **Examples**: Streams of the Saurashtra region, Central French Plateau, Mt. Kilimanjaro.
 
 
 
• **Trellis**__
 
 
• In this type of pattern, the short subsequent streams meet the mainstream at right angles, and differential erosion through soft rocks paves the way for tributaries.
 
• Examples: The old folded mountains of the **Singhbhum (Chotanagpur Plateau**) and the Seine and its tributaries in the Paris basin (France) have drainage of trellis pattern.

questions.question: Bokajan is a cement plant located in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bokajan** is a cement plant **located **in the **Karbi Anglong district of Assam**, situated approximately 21 kilometers from Dimapur Airport and 350 kilometers from Guwahati.
 
• It is **operated by **the **Cement Corporation of India Limited (CCI)**.
 
• It is one of the 3 functional cement factory in India, out of its 10 cement factories of CCI, which are fully owned by the Central Govt. of India.
 
• Annually, the plant produces around 198,000 MT by using the dry process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cement**: 

 
 
• It is a **binding material** that hardens when mixed with water, sand, and gravel to form concrete.
 
• It plays a crucial role in construction due to its strength, durability, and versatility.
 
• Based on how they set and harden, cement materials can be divided into** two categories**: hydraulic cements and non-hydraulic cements respectively.
 
 
• **Hydraulic cements**: The** dry materials and water** in hydraulic cements, such as Portland cement, **react chemically to set and become adhesive**.
 
• **Non-hydraulic cement**: Less often used non-hydraulic cement **does not harden in damp environments or underwater**.
 
 
• Instead, it **solidifies when it dries and interacts with atmospheric carbon dioxide**.

questions.question: The Walayar Dam is in which district of Kerala?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3,i.e. Palakkad.

__
 
• Walayar Dam is a dam in **Palakkad district**__ of Kerala, South India.
 
• This dam is constructed across the Walayar River which is a tributary of Kalpathipuzha River.
 
• It was completed and opened in 1964.
 
• It is one of the major sources of irrigation in the region.

questions.question: Which of the following states has one of the richest monazite deposits in India?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64e177b3c5c5cb81c12b3d5b5ddabaaf474cdad3d6098992ca6592786c8147d6.png] 

 
• **World’s richest monazite deposits **occur in the** Palakkad and Kollam districts of Kerala.**
 
• Nuclear minerals are **abundant in India** to meet its future energy demand.
 
• Nuclear mineral in India primarily **comprises of the Thorium and very few reserves of Uranium.**
 
• Thorium is mainly obtained from **monazite and ilmenite along the coast of Kerala and Tamil Nadu**, where it is available in abundance.
 
• Over **15,200 tonnes of uranium** is estimated to be contained in **monazite**.

questions.question: What is the name of the first crude oil pipeline constructed in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Naharkatia-Nunmati-Barauni Pipeline.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This was the** first pipeline constructed** in India to bring crude oil from** Naharkatia (Assam) oilfield to Nunmati (Assam)**.
 
• It was extended to transport crude oil** to the refinery at Barauni in Bihar.** 
 
• Total Length of the pipeline** 1167 km.**
 
• It is **now extended to Kanpur in Uttar Pradesh.**
 
• The pipeline between **Naharkatia and Nunmati became operative in 1962 **and that between **Nunmati and Barauni in 1964.**

**​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Mumbai High-Mumbai-Ankleshwar-Kayoli Pipeline is a **210 km long double-pipeline that connects Mumbai with Mumbai High**.

 
 
• **Ankleshwar-Koyali pipeline** was completed in **1965.**
 
• It transports crude oil from Ankleshwar oilfield to the Koyali refinery.
 
 
 
• Hajira-Bijapur-Jagdishpur (HBJ) Gas Pipeline is the** longest pipeline** of India having a length of **1750 km.**
 
 
• It was established by the Gas Authority of India.
